aif-c01.overview: Build foundational AI literacy across all five AIF-C01 domains, with a lesson on foundation model applications and offline exercises for the remaining topics.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with cloud services and business workflows
Comfort reading a simple chart or metric

topics: AI vs ML vs deep learning
modules.objective: Classify an AI use case and explain how its data and success criteria influence the approach.
modules.exercise: Write three business problems. For each, identify the prediction or generation task, available labels, one success metric, and one reason a non-AI solution might suffice.

modules.objective: Explain how a foundation model generates output and compare options using capability, cost, and risk.
modules.exercise: Draw a prompt-to-response flow. Compare a small text model and a multimodal model for two fictional requests, documenting the missing information needed to choose.

modules.objective: Choose prompting, retrieval, or customization to address a specific output problem.
modules.exercise: Use a three-paragraph fictional policy to draft a grounded prompt. Write an answerable question and an unanswerable one, plus the expected citation or abstention; no model call is required.

modules.objective: Identify affected users and propose measurable responsible AI safeguards.
modules.exercise: Create a risk table for a résumé-screening assistant. Include three possible harms, evidence needed to detect each, a mitigation, and the person responsible for review.

modules.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
modules.objective: Connect an AI data-flow risk to an access, privacy, or governance control.
modules.exercise: Sketch a support chatbot data flow. Mark where personal data enters, who can read it, what is logged, and when it is deleted. Explain which controls belong to the application team.

aip-c01.overview: Study all five AIP-C01 domains through domain lessons, decision-focused topic outlines, and offline architecture and evaluation exercises.
prerequisites: HTTP APIs, JSON, and basic application architecture
IAM roles, storage, and networking fundamentals
Basic prompting and retrieval augmented generation

modules.objective: Design a model and retrieval approach that satisfies business, data, and compliance constraints.
modules.exercise: Using a fictional support manual, specify chunk boundaries, metadata filters, an access rule, and five evaluation questions. Explain how you would handle conflicting or missing evidence.

modules.objective: Trace a complete model-to-tool workflow with authorization, retries, and explicit failure handling.
modules.exercise: Write pseudocode for a refund assistant: validate the request, request approval, execute one authorized tool, deduplicate retries, and return the result. Walk through a timeout after the refund succeeds.

modules.objective: Select layered controls for an AI workflow and identify what each control cannot guarantee.
modules.exercise: Threat-model a document assistant. Write one malicious retrieved passage, then specify input separation, retrieval authorization, tool restrictions, and audit events that contain its effects.

modules.objective: Compare inference options against measured traffic, latency, quality, and budget requirements.
modules.exercise: Create a spreadsheet or paper estimate for 1,000 fictional requests. Vary input tokens, output tokens, cache hit rate, and model price assumptions; label assumed prices and identify the largest cost driver.

modules.objective: Use a repeatable evaluation to isolate a failure and decide whether a change is safe to release.
modules.exercise: Build a six-case evaluation table including missing evidence, conflicting evidence, unsafe requests, and malformed tool results. Define pass criteria and a rollback trigger before proposing a prompt change.

ans-c01.overview: Review advanced AWS networking through all four ANS-C01 domains. AWS has announced exam retirement after December 31, 2026; this outline remains useful for networking study.
prerequisites: IP addressing, subnetting, routing, and DNS
AWS VPC and hybrid connectivity fundamentals
Experience interpreting network diagrams

modules.objective: Design a hybrid network whose routing and failure behavior meet stated requirements.
modules.exercise: Draw two data centers and two AWS Regions. Mark redundant links, route advertisements, DNS resolution paths, and a single-link failure; explain the expected surviving path.

modules.objective: Translate a network design into an ordered implementation and validation plan.
modules.exercise: Write a configuration checklist for connecting two fictional VPCs through a transit gateway. List required routes, attachment associations, security rules, and reachability checks without creating resources.

modules.objective: Isolate a network fault using routing, DNS, policy, and traffic evidence.
modules.exercise: Invent a failed HTTPS request across a hybrid link. Build a diagnostic sequence covering DNS, routes, security groups, network ACLs, and return paths; note what evidence would eliminate each cause.

modules.objective: Place security controls along a traffic path while preserving required connectivity.
modules.exercise: Annotate a three-tier network diagram with trust boundaries and permitted flows. Add a centralized inspection hop and trace both outbound and return traffic for asymmetric routing risks.

clf-c02.overview: Learn the cloud concepts, security responsibilities, service choices, and billing fundamentals in CLF-C02, with an available cloud technology lesson.
prerequisites: Basic computer and internet literacy
No prior certification required for this outline

modules.objective: Explain how cloud characteristics address a business requirement.
modules.exercise: For a seasonal shop, a global website, and an internal payroll system, identify a cloud benefit and a tradeoff; distinguish scaling from improving availability.

modules.objective: Assign security responsibilities and choose a suitable foundational control.
modules.exercise: Make an AWS-versus-customer responsibility table for virtual machines and managed databases. Include operating-system patching, data classification, access control, and physical security.

modules.objective: Select a service category from a simple workload description and justify the fit.
modules.exercise: Create a service map for a fictional photo-sharing app: uploads, metadata, image processing, delivery, and monitoring. Compare one alternative for each component.

modules.objective: Identify the billing or support mechanism that addresses a stated operational need.
modules.exercise: Draft a monthly cost-review checklist for three teams. Include tags, unusual-spend alerts, idle resources, support escalation, and one workload suitable for a commitment discount.

dea-c01.overview: Work through the four DEA-C01 domains from ingestion to governance, using pipeline design exercises and an ingestion lesson.
prerequisites: Basic SQL and data modeling
Batch and streaming pipeline concepts
AWS storage and IAM fundamentals

modules.objective: Design an ingestion pipeline that preserves correctness through retries and changing data.
modules.exercise: Sketch a pipeline for daily CSV orders and streaming status events. Define keys, deduplication, schema-change handling, a bad-record path, and a reconciliation count.

modules.objective: Choose a storage layout that supports query patterns, governance, and cost constraints.
modules.exercise: Design a local folder layout for one year of fictional sales data. Specify partition keys, file format, retention, and two query patterns; explain the small-file risk.

modules.objective: Use pipeline and query evidence to distinguish freshness, correctness, and performance problems.
modules.exercise: Given an invented pipeline that completes on time but loses 5% of rows, write checks at each stage. Then add a separate slow-query symptom and identify which evidence would differentiate the causes.

modules.objective: Apply access and protection rules consistently across a data pipeline.
modules.exercise: Create an access matrix for raw, curated, and analytics datasets. Include an engineer, analyst, and service role; mark sensitive columns and record one audit event for each privileged operation.

dop-c02.overview: Organize professional DevOps study across delivery, infrastructure, resilience, observability, incidents, and governance; an SDLC automation lesson is available.
prerequisites: Software delivery and source control
AWS operations, IAM, and networking fundamentals
Basic scripting and infrastructure as code

modules.objective: Design a repeatable delivery pipeline that prevents unsafe promotion and supports recovery.
modules.exercise: Write a pipeline outline for a small API. Identify immutable artifacts, test gates, deployment approval, a canary metric, and the exact rollback condition.

modules.objective: Separate infrastructure, runtime configuration, and secrets while managing drift.
modules.exercise: Draft a repository layout with shared infrastructure modules and dev/prod parameters. Describe how to detect a manual change and restore the declared state without putting secrets in source control.

modules.objective: Match a resilience design to recovery objectives and failure scenarios.
modules.exercise: Set fictional RTO and RPO targets for a payment API. Draw the recovery plan, list dependency failures, and describe a safe tabletop failover exercise with success criteria.

modules.objective: Create observability signals that reveal user impact and support diagnosis.
modules.exercise: Define an availability indicator, latency indicator, dashboard, and actionable alarm for an API. Trace one incident from the user symptom to a log field and an ownership route.

modules.objective: Design an incident response that limits impact and verifies recovery.
modules.exercise: Write a runbook for a failed deployment causing elevated errors. Include evidence collection, rollback decision, idempotent remediation, validation, and a short post-incident improvement.

modules.objective: Protect the software delivery path and collect evidence for its controls.
modules.exercise: Threat-model a build pipeline from source to production. Identify where credentials could leak, who can change release gates, and what evidence would prove a signed artifact was deployed.

dva-c02.overview: Build an AWS application-development study plan across implementation, security, deployment, and troubleshooting, with a service-development lesson.
prerequisites: Programming and HTTP API fundamentals
Basic databases, queues, and AWS services
Familiarity with testing and source control

modules.objective: Implement a service interaction that remains correct through duplicates, retries, and partial failure.
modules.exercise: Write pseudocode for processing an order event twice. Include an idempotency key, conditional write, retriable error, and dead-letter path; trace the state after each step.

modules.objective: Choose application security controls that restrict both callers and workload permissions.
modules.exercise: Design access rules for a browser, API, and background worker. Identify which identity calls each service, where authorization runs, and how a secret rotates without entering the client bundle.

modules.objective: Plan a deployment that keeps code, configuration, and rollback versions consistent.
modules.exercise: Draft a release checklist for a serverless API. Include dependency packaging, environment settings, a staged traffic shift, smoke checks, and the prior version needed for rollback.

modules.objective: Use observable evidence to distinguish application faults from dependency or capacity limits.
modules.exercise: Create a timeline for a request that retries a throttled dependency and exceeds its timeout. Mark useful logs and metrics, then propose a bounded retry policy and a verification step.

genai-engineer.overview: Outline the six Databricks Generative AI Engineer Associate domains using the official March 2026 guide, with an application-development lesson and offline design exercises.
prerequisites: Basic Python and API concepts
LLM prompting and retrieval fundamentals
Familiarity with data pipelines and access control

modules.objective: Translate a business task into an application design with measurable output requirements.
modules.exercise: Define a fictional internal FAQ assistant. Write its inputs, required output schema, allowed tools, unsupported requests, and five acceptance examples before selecting a model.

modules.objective: Prepare a retrieval dataset and explain how preprocessing choices affect answer quality.
modules.exercise: Split a short local policy document into chunks on paper. Assign source IDs and access metadata, write three search queries, and explain which relevant passage each query should retrieve.

modules.objective: Connect application components into a testable RAG or agent workflow.
modules.exercise: Write a local pseudocode pipeline for retrieve, assemble context, generate, and validate. Add one malicious passage and one empty retrieval result, then trace the expected safe output for each.

modules.objective: Describe how an application is packaged, authorized, served, and updated.
modules.exercise: Draw an application-to-serving architecture with a retrieval index and one tool. Mark service identities, secret boundaries, versioned artifacts, and a rollback path; no Databricks workspace is required.

modules.objective: Choose governance controls for both application inputs and source data.
modules.exercise: Make a review checklist for three fictional sources: an internal manual, customer messages, and a licensed article. Decide permitted uses, redaction needs, access restrictions, and evidence to retain.

modules.objective: Design an evaluation and monitoring loop that identifies actionable quality regressions.
modules.exercise: Create a six-row evaluation dataset with expected evidence and scoring criteria. Include one judge that needs a reference answer and one that does not; define a drift signal and a review threshold.

genai-leader.overview: Connect generative AI fundamentals and Google Cloud offerings to practical business decisions, with a lesson on Google Cloud offerings.
prerequisites: Basic business processes and outcome measurement
No hands-on cloud experience required for these exercises

modules.objective: Explain generative AI to a business stakeholder with clear capabilities and limitations.
modules.exercise: Describe three potential workplace uses in plain language. For each, name the input, output, business benefit, failure risk, and the human review needed before acting.

modules.objective: Match Google Cloud offerings to a business need and identify when specialist help is required.
modules.exercise: Build a decision table for document summarization, enterprise search, and workflow assistance. Compare the relevant Google Cloud offering, data requirements, and operational responsibility using the official guide.

modules.domain: Techniques to improve gen AI model output
modules.objective: Choose a practical method for improving model output based on the observed weakness.
modules.exercise: Rewrite a vague meeting-summary prompt with an audience, format, evidence requirement, and examples. Write expected outputs for an incomplete transcript and a transcript containing conflicting statements.

modules.domain: Business strategies for a successful gen AI solution
modules.objective: Propose an AI pilot with a business owner, measurable outcome, and review gates.
modules.exercise: Prepare a one-page pilot plan for a fictional support team. Define baseline workload, a success metric, costs to track, privacy constraints, staff training, and a stop-or-expand decision.

mla-c01.overview: Study the legacy MLA-C01 blueprint retained by this English practice bank. English MLA-C01 testing ended September 28, 2026; this outline is not an MLA-C02 course. Use the official exam page to review the successor before booking.
prerequisites: Basic ML training and evaluation
Data preparation and Python concepts
AWS IAM, storage, and SageMaker fundamentals

modules.objective: Prepare a reproducible dataset for the legacy MLA-C01 workflow without leaking target information.
modules.exercise: Create a ten-row fictional customer dataset. Mark the label, missing values, sensitive fields, and features unavailable at prediction time; choose a time-aware split and explain your leakage checks.

modules.objective: Choose and evaluate a training approach using the problem type and error costs.
modules.exercise: Build a small confusion matrix on paper for fraud predictions. Calculate precision and recall, explain the business tradeoff, and specify a training experiment that would test a proposed improvement.

modules.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
modules.objective: Plan model deployment and promotion with explicit validation and rollback steps.
modules.exercise: Draw a training-to-deployment workflow with artifact registration, an approval gate, staged traffic, and rollback. Compare online and batch inference for a fictional daily scoring job.

modules.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
modules.objective: Define monitoring and security controls for a deployed legacy ML workload.
modules.exercise: Write a monitoring sheet with input drift, quality, latency, and access signals. For each, specify evidence, an owner, and a response; explain why drift alone does not prove that retraining helps.

nca-genl.overview: Build foundational LLM knowledge across all five NCA-GENL topic areas. The available NVIDIA stack lesson links model fundamentals to software delivery.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of generative AI and LLMs
Introductory Python and data concepts

modules.domain: Core Machine Learning and AI Knowledge
modules.objective: Explain the components of an LLM application and distinguish generation from retrieval.
modules.exercise: Draw a document-question-answer flow. Label tokenization, embedding, retrieval, prompt assembly, and generation; explain how an incorrect retrieved passage can produce a plausible wrong answer.

modules.objective: Describe how a model becomes an application service with defined inputs and failure behavior.
modules.exercise: Write pseudocode for a chat API wrapper with input limits, a timeout, structured output validation, and a mocked response. Identify where serving optimizations could help and what must be measured.

modules.objective: Compare experiments while keeping evaluation conditions and evidence consistent.
modules.exercise: Plan two prompt variants against the same ten fictional requests. Record the hypothesis, fixed conditions, evaluation rubric, and decision rule; explain why changing the test set mid-comparison weakens the result.

modules.objective: Interpret data and evaluation results without overlooking sampling or measurement limits.
modules.exercise: Use ten invented latency values and ten quality labels. Compute the average, identify an outlier, sketch a chart, and explain which additional data you need before choosing a model.

modules.objective: Identify an AI trust risk and propose a testable mitigation.
modules.exercise: Review a fictional public chatbot. Write three misuse or privacy scenarios, the data required to test each, one mitigation, and a human escalation rule.

saa-c03.overview: Practice architecture decisions across security, resilience, performance, and cost, with a lesson on secure architectures.
prerequisites: AWS compute, storage, database, and networking basics
IAM and shared-responsibility fundamentals

modules.objective: Design workload boundaries that protect access, traffic, and stored data.
modules.exercise: Sketch a web application with public and private components. Label roles, allowed network flows, encrypted data, and audit logs; explain how an administrator connects without public inbound access.

modules.objective: Choose resilient patterns based on failure scope and recovery objectives.
modules.exercise: Draw a two-AZ service and list what happens when an instance, database node, or AZ fails. Set fictional RTO/RPO goals and identify the backup or failover evidence needed to meet them.

modules.objective: Select performance improvements that address a measured bottleneck.
modules.exercise: Given a fictional API with slow database reads and globally distant users, separate compute, data, and network hypotheses. Choose a measurement and architecture option for each rather than scaling everything.

modules.objective: Reduce cost while maintaining the workload requirements that matter.
modules.exercise: Make a cost-optimization proposal for a batch job and a steady API. Compare purchase options, idle capacity, storage retention, and transfer paths; document any availability or latency tradeoff.

sap-c02.overview: Structure advanced architecture study around organizational complexity, new solutions, improvement, and migration, with a lesson on new solution design.
prerequisites: Practical AWS architecture experience
Multi-account, networking, and security fundamentals
Ability to reason about recovery and consistency tradeoffs

modules.objective: Design common controls for multiple business units with distinct ownership boundaries.
modules.exercise: Create an account and organizational-unit diagram for a fictional enterprise. Assign identity, network, security, and application responsibilities; trace one cross-account access request.

modules.objective: Select a new architecture that satisfies competing functional and operational constraints.
modules.exercise: Write an architecture decision for a global ordering service. Include traffic shape, consistency, latency, RTO/RPO, security, and cost; compare two designs and explain the rejected option.

modules.objective: Prioritize improvements using evidence from an existing system and measurable acceptance criteria.
modules.exercise: Invent a legacy application with one outage pattern, one bottleneck, and one cost issue. Rank three improvements, identify dependencies, and define a before/after measure for each.

modules.objective: Plan a migration that controls data consistency, downtime, and recovery risk.
modules.exercise: Draft a staged migration plan for a database-backed application. Include dependency discovery, initial copy, change synchronization, cutover checks, rollback conditions, and post-cutover reconciliation.

scs-c03.overview: Study the six SCS-C03 security domains through control-selection and incident exercises, with an available IAM lesson.
prerequisites: AWS IAM, networking, and logging fundamentals
Basic incident response and security concepts
Experience reasoning about data protection

modules.objective: Connect a suspicious event to the logging and detection evidence needed to investigate it.
modules.exercise: Construct a fictional sequence of unusual sign-ins and data reads. List relevant audit fields, a detection rule, false-positive checks, and the account or team that should receive the finding.

modules.objective: Design an incident response that limits damage while preserving evidence.
modules.exercise: Write a tabletop runbook for a compromised workload role. Order containment, credential response, forensic capture, scope checks, and recovery; identify one automated step that needs safeguards.

modules.objective: Choose infrastructure controls that reduce exposure across network and compute layers.
modules.exercise: Review a fictional internet-facing service diagram. Mark public entry points, unnecessary traffic, patching responsibilities, and protective controls; trace how an attacker could reach a private datastore.

modules.objective: Evaluate an access request across granting and restricting policy layers.
modules.exercise: Write a policy-evaluation table for a role reading a cross-account bucket. Add an explicit deny, a permission boundary, and an SCP one at a time; explain which requests remain authorized.

topics: Encryption at rest and in transit
modules.objective: Design data protection with clear ownership of keys, permissions, and retention.
modules.exercise: Map a sensitive document from upload through storage, processing, backup, and deletion. Specify encryption, key access, audit events, retention, and the evidence needed to verify deletion scope.

modules.objective: Translate security requirements into preventive controls and reviewable evidence.
modules.exercise: Create a control register for a fictional three-account organization. Include requirement, owner, enforcement mechanism, evidence, review cadence, and one time-limited exception with compensating controls.

soa-c03.overview: Plan CloudOps study across monitoring, recovery, automation, security, and networking, with a lesson on monitoring and remediation.
prerequisites: AWS compute, networking, and storage basics
Basic monitoring and incident troubleshooting
Familiarity with command-line operations and IAM

modules.domain: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
modules.objective: Diagnose an operational symptom and design a measured, reversible remediation.
modules.exercise: Create an incident timeline for an API with rising latency and errors. Define a dashboard, a composite alarm idea, diagnostic queries, and a remediation step with a recovery check.

modules.objective: Operate a workload through failure while meeting recovery and data-loss limits.
modules.exercise: Write a restore runbook for a fictional database. State RTO/RPO, backup selection, dependency restoration order, data validation, and a tabletop test that would expose an unusable backup.

modules.objective: Plan repeatable infrastructure and configuration changes with safe recovery.
modules.exercise: Draft a patch rollout for a two-AZ service. Include inventory, a small first group, health checks, approval conditions, drift handling, and a rollback or replacement plan.

modules.objective: Maintain access and security controls while responding to operational findings.
modules.exercise: Build a checklist for onboarding a workload role and later removing its access. Include trust, least privilege, secret handling, logging, and a review of unused permissions.

modules.objective: Trace an application request through DNS, network controls, routing, and delivery layers.
modules.exercise: Diagram a request from a user through DNS, a CDN, a load balancer, and a private instance. Introduce a missing route and a blocked port separately, then identify the evidence that distinguishes them.
